'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**[[2022 Bannu counterterrorism centre attack and siege]]
***Security forces storm a [[counterterrorism]] office in [[Bannu]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]], which was seized two days ago by 33 [[Pakistani Taliban]] members, killing all of the [[insurgent]]s. Two officers were killed during the [[siege]] and many others were injured. All of the [[hostage]]s are freed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-64041270 (BBC News)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**At least 38 people are killed and several houses are [[arson|torched]] during two attacks at two villages in [[Kagoro]], [[Kaduna State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://allafrica.com/stories/202212210024.html (All Africa)]
*[[Sino-Indian border dispute]]
**[[India]] reports that it has increased its [[Indian Army|troop]] presence along the [[Sino-Indian border]] in response to the [[skirmish]] that occurred between Indian and [[Chinese troops]] in [[Tawang district]] earlier this month. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/india-claims-to-maintain-troop-deployment-like-never-before-on-china-border/ar-AA15uhVw?ocid=entnewsntp&cvid=5322bc56b4064d97919459b9627226db (MSN)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Ferndale earthquake]]
**A magnitude 6.4 [[list of earthquakes in California|earthquake]] strikes [[Humboldt County, California]], [[United States]], killing at least two people, injuring eleven others and causing minor damage. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/rcna62522 (NBC News)]
*[[2022 Urengoy–Pomary–Uzhhorod pipeline explosion]]
**An [[explosion]] occurs on an [[Urengoy–Pomary–Uzhhorod pipeline|Urengoy–Pomary–Uzhhorod export gas pipeline]] during maintenance work in [[Chuvashia]], [[Russia]], killing three workers and causing a stoppage of gas flows through the pipeline. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/blast-west-kazan-shuts-russia-ukraine-gas-export-pipeline-2022-12-20/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Mexico–Peru relations]]
**[[Mexico]] confirms that it has granted asylum to the family of former [[Peruvian president]] [[Pedro Castillo]], with [[Secretary of Foreign Affairs (Mexico)|Foreign Minister]] [[Marcelo Ebrard]] saying that a safe exit from [[Peru]] is currently being discussed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-says-has-granted-asylum-family-perus-castillo-2022-12-20/ (Reuters)]
**Peru expels the Mexican ambassador and declares him [[persona non grata]] hours after Mexico grants asylum to the family of former Peruvian president Pedro Castillo. [https://apnews.com/article/mexico-peru-caribbean-lima-children-4c3ac672a24c1cb488418f227948e877 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Treatment of women by the Taliban]]
**The [[Taliban]] ban university education for women in [[Afghanistan]]. A spokesman for the [[Ministry of Higher Education (Afghanistan)|Ministry of Higher Education]] says that the decree was issued by the [[Cabinet of Afghanistan|Cabinet]] today and entered into force effective immediately. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/12/20/asia/taliban-bans-women-university-education-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Science and technology'''
*Argentine [[Football player|footballer]] [[Lionel Messi]]'s [[Instagram]] post containing photos of him lifting the [[FIFA World Cup Trophy]] and celebrating with the [[Argentina national football team|Argentina team]] after winning the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] two days prior becomes [[List of most-liked Instagram posts|the social networking service's most-liked post]] after reaching over 56 million [[Like button#Instagram|likes]], surpassing the previous record held by the [[Instagram egg]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-64003233 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022–23 PGA Tour]]
**[[Augusta National Golf Club]] chairperson [[Fred Ridley]] announces that [[professional golfer]]s who are signed under the [[LIV Golf]] [[Professional golf tours|tour]], which began [[2022 LIV Golf Invitational Series |this year]] as a competitor to the [[PGA Tour]], will be permitted to play in the [[2023 Masters Tournament]], the first of four [[men's major golf championships]] held next year. Human rights groups and various personalities have criticized LIV Golf, which is financed by [[Saudi Arabia]]'s [[Public Investment Fund]], as a [[sportswashing]] project by the country to improve its [[Human rights in Saudi Arabia|repressive]] global image. [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/golf/masters-liv-golf-2023-entry-criteria-b2248746.html (''The Independent'')]
